description: Disable the Vibes button in the pool _InputBar (mission_room.dart) so it is no longer reachable from the UI. The _onSendVibe method can stay in code but the button should be hidden/inactive.
steps: In mission_room.dart around line 1569-1590, comment out or remove the Vibe button block (the if-statement checking widget.onSendVibe != null && widget.poolId != null and its child GestureDetector with the gift icon). The simplest approach: wrap the entire vibe button block in a `if (false)` guard or just remove it from the widget tree. Keep the onSendVibe field in the _InputBar constructor so the method reference does not break, but make the button invisible.
Alternatively, change the condition to always false: replace `if (widget.onSendVibe != null && widget.poolId != null)` with `if (false)` to disable it without removing the code structure.
acceptance_criteria: The vibe/gift button does not appear in the input bar UI (either hidden via false condition or removed from widget tree)
The _onSendVibe method still exists in mission_room.dart (not deleted)
The onSendVibe parameter in _InputBar constructor still exists (no breaking signature changes)
No compile errors introduced (the field is still declared and passed but UI just never shows it)
verification: Run grep to confirm the vibe button conditional is disabled (either 'if (false)' or the GestureDetector block is removed/commented)
Run grep to confirm _onSendVibe method still exists in mission_room.dart
Run grep to confirm onSendVibe field still exists in _InputBar
findings: Changed condition from 'if (widget.onSendVibe != null && widget.poolId != null)' to 'if (false && widget.onSendVibe != null && widget.poolId != null)' at line 1570. Added comment indicating temporary disable for design parity and dead_code ignore annotation. All acceptance criteria verified via grep: method, parameter, and call site preserved.
